messages:
Raj K: Heads up — seeing repeated TX queue stalls and RX overruns on a2-highmem in us-west-2 after the kernel upgrade to 6.2. Apps report east-west latency spikes and some pod restarts.
Nicole H: How widespread? which ASGs/ami?
Raj K: ~12 nodes across asg-worker-a2-{usw2-a,usw2-b}. AMI: rdi-a2-highmem-2026-03 (MTU 9001). Pattern: high pps batch jobs hit the nodes, then doorbell timeouts.
Dmitri P: ENA or MLX5? any specific dmesg lines?
Raj K: ENA. dmesg repeatedly: `ena 0000:03:00.0: tx timeout: doorbell timeout` and RX overruns. Quick ethtool -S snippet we grabbed: 
```
ethtool -S eth0 | egrep 'rx_over|tx_doorbell|tx_queue'
rx_over_errors: 4821
tx_queue_stopped: 6
tx_doorbell_timeout: 14
```
Maya L: MTU 9001 + jumbo frames + a driver/firmware mismatch can cause fragmentation/RSS desync. Did the kernel change any offload code?
Raj K: Kernel 6.2 came from infra base; we didn't touch offloads explicitly. We do see an uptick in NetworkRxDropped at ENI level in CloudWatch aligned to the timestamps.
Nicole H: Any other instance types seeing this?
Raj K: No, only a2-highmem so far. Same AMI across other regions with older kernel looks fine.
Infra Bot: :warning: anomaly detected for asg-worker-a2-highmem-usw2 - https://monitoring.internal/alerts/9271
Bob S: Can you try toggling MTU to 1500 on a canary node and repro? If it disappears that's a strong hint.
Raj K: Will try. Also attempted rmmod/insmod of ena and soft NIC reset — transiently reduced errors but they came back after ~30m.
Dmitri P: If reload helps briefly then firmware might be dropping workqueues under load. Which ena driver version + fw?
Raj K: Driver: ena 2.3.5, kernel module built-in from distro. FW reported as 2.1.0-rc. We have mixed firmware versions across the fleet (some older nodes show 2.0.x).
Maya L: Mixed firmware + new kernel = perfect storm. Can we quarantine the newer-fw nodes from the autoscaler?
Carol T: I'll create an autoscaler tag rule to avoid launching new instances with that AMI and schedule a rolling drain of affected nodes.
Nicole H: Opened internal ticket ID INF-3942 and pinged the cloud vendor rep. Include ethtool/dmesg samples.
Bob S: Vendor ticket is good. Also prepare a rollback AMI (kernel 5.x or older ena driver) as contingency.
Raj K: Quick canary: switched one node MTU->1500 and restarted workload — no immediate doorbell hits for 18m, but still collecting.
Maya L: Tests to run: 1) MTU 1500 vs 9001, 2) pin traffic to single queue to see if RSS is the problem, 3) reimage with older firmware if vendor provides.
Raj K: Agreed. I'll also run a small txrx load test with iperf at pps levels to repro.
Infra Bot: Action items logged: INF-3942 assigned to Raj K, priority P1.
Nicole H: Thanks — keep updates here. If vendor confirms firmware regression we need emergency AMI freeze and rollback plan. :thumbsup:
Raj K: Will update when I have iperf logs and vendor response.
Carol T: I'll schedule the drain window for tonight 02:00-04:00 UTC and add a runbook.
Bob S: If anyone needs me to open a support escalation, ping and I'll do it.
Dmitri P: FYI also check NIC MSI/MSI-X interrupt counts; if those are getting backed up that's another signal.
Raj K: Noted, will capture /proc/interrupts and share. Thanks everyone.
